_readme: Magic, played rather than unit-tested: the Magic command, an attack spell, a heal, a
refusal the purse causes, and the swing that finishes the job anyway.
The refusal is the leg that could not be written any other way. BattleLogic proves that
a cast beyond the MP is refused; only a played fight proves the player can still DO
something afterwards - that the refusal costs no turn, leaves the page up, and lets a
cancel back out onto a command that works. A rule that stranded the player there would
pass every unit test in the file.
The numbers are exact and deterministic: 8 MP at level 1, Ember costs 3, Mend costs 4,
so the second Ember is one point short. Slink's moves are drawn from the fight's own
seed, so its damage varies with nothing - but hp is left unasserted anyway, because
what this script is about is the magic, and MP and the win are what say it worked.

steps.text: the warden opens the game - hear her out first
a player who has never fought is filled in from the curve, magic included - 8 at level 1
west into the hollow, straight into the thing standing in the gap
Rows: Attack, Magic, Item, Flee. Magic is the second, so one down then confirm. The spell page is what the player has REACHED: Ember and Mend at level 1, and no Lull, which arrives at 2.
Ember first: 3 MP, and its damage ignores the slink's armour
hurt now, so Mend: 4 MP, which leaves one - not enough for anything
and now the leg this script exists for: one point short of an Ember. The cast is refused, it is SAID, and it costs no turn - so backing out onto Attack has to still be there to do.
out of the spells, back up onto Attack, and finish it with a swing
8 - 3 - 4 = 1, and the refused cast took nothing. A fight that charged for the refusal would say 0 here, and one that never spent anything would say 8.
five xp is not a level, so nothing refilled the magic on the way out
